justify-start">There are also <i class="font-italic">artificial light sources</i> like controlled fires, gas lamps, incandescent light bulbs... and in the 21st century, there's energy-efficient fluorescent lights and LED lighting.</p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">However, this is not just a story of technology and progress. The light bulb did not make the sun obsolete, and the LED does not make fire obsolete. We still like sunny days and romantic candle-lit dinners. </p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">Fire has not disappeared from the world. Instead, the meaning and use of fire has changed. Lighting design is about understanding how light conveys these ideas, moods, and emotions.</p><div class="decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl layout-wide:max-w-6xl mx-auto print:break-inside-avoid flex visible plausible source of light, like a light bulb or a fireplace. But a window with sunlight is also like a fixture. Within a game level, this is usually like an architectural feature or a decorative lamp prop. </p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">This is not the same as an in-engine light source, which is actually an invisible source of light with no apparent cause. self-start justify-start">A <strong class="font-bold">motivated light</strong> is a light source with a plausible fixture. </p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">Note that a <i class="font-italic">single fixture may actually motivate multiple invisible in-engine light sources. print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start"><strong class="font-bold">Lighting</strong> gives visual depth to a scene, allowing players to gauge distances and distinguish shapes. Because it serves a very important gameplay function, you should do a <strong class="font-bold">lighting pass</strong> early in the level design process, before a proper art pass.</p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">Video game lighting tech is a crude illusion that approximates real-life light. Many game lighting effects do not actually use any lighting systems.</p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">There are 4 core light source types: <strong class="font-bold">ambient, directional, point, and spotlight. </strong>These lights can be <i class="font-italic">static </i>or <i class="font-italic">dynamic, </i>and <strong class="font-bold">motivated</strong> by a visible <strong class="font-bold">light fixture</strong> or <i class="font-italic">unmotivated</i> without any visible source.</p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">The most common lighting theory is three point lighting, which defines <strong class="font-bold">key lights</strong>, <strong class="font-bold">fill lights</strong>, and <strong class="font-bold">rim lights </strong>based on the light's orientation to the camera and subject.</p><p data-cover-aware-text="" class="paragraph decoration-primary/6 max-w-3xl w-full print:break-inside-avoid text-start self-start justify-start">To light a level, work gradually over several lighting passes. Do global lights first, then light for wayfinding, and then for gameplay, and finally any last details or moods.</p><h2 id="now-what" class="text-xl @xs:text-2xl @lg:text-3xl font-semibold heading
